tasks.title: Single-correct quizzes must use replace (radio) selection, plus two verification-integrity fixes
tasks.prompt:
You are implementing the single fix task that stands between milestone M2 and its sign-off.
Repository root: /home/mrcolson/repos/casio-sxc1. You own exactly these paths:

    /home/mrcolson/repos/casio-sxc1/site/src/SXC1/Exercise/Engine.hs
    /home/mrcolson/repos/casio-sxc1/site/test/CheckExercises.hs

    /home/mrcolson/repos/casio-sxc1/scripts/check-site.sh

Do not create or edit anything else. In particular do NOT touch content/, site/app/View/Exercise.hs,
site/static/index.html, or any other library module unless a compile error forces it -- and if one does,
stop and report rather than widening scope.

Activate the toolchain with `. "$HOME/.ghc-wasm/env"`. Build with -j2. A cold build can exceed a
10-minute foreground timeout: run it as a BACKGROUND command teed to a log and poll the log.

=============================================================================
FIX 1 (BLOCKING, learner-facing) -- single-correct quizzes must REPLACE, not ADD
=============================================================================
I drove the real app during sign-off and found this by walking the ordinary learner path:

    q-1-03 has four options, exactly one correct (opt-a).
    click opt-b            -> opt-b=true
    click opt-a            -> opt-a=true AND opt-b=true      <-- both stay selected
    submit                 -> "Not quite. Try again."        <-- while the CORRECT answer is visibly selected
    click opt-b (deselect) -> submit -> "Correct."

That is a misgrade from the learner's point of view: they clicked the right answer and were told they
were wrong. It is the milestone's headline interaction ("an answer path works"), so it blocks sign-off.

The grading rule is NOT wrong and must not change: `Choice` is correct iff the selected option-id SET
equals the correct SET exactly. What is missing is SELECTION semantics, which my manifest never specified.
Add them in SXC1.Exercise.Engine's `Toggle` handler:

  * If the prompt has exactly ONE correct option (single-answer), `Toggle i optIdent` REPLACES the
    selection with [optIdent]. Re-clicking the already-selected option still clears it (so a learner can
    unselect), but selecting any other option never leaves two pressed.
  * If the prompt has TWO OR MORE correct options (multi-select), `Toggle` keeps today's additive
    behaviour unchanged -- that is genuinely a multi-select control.

The arity is already available from the Exercise's own `pcOptions` (count `optCorrect`), so this is a
decision the engine can make with no format change, no view change and no new field. `step` stays pure
and total.

Add to exercise-check --self-test, in the group that already covers Choice grading, cases that pin BOTH
branches and would fail against today's code:
  * single-correct: Toggle b, then Toggle a  => selection is exactly [a]; Submit grades Correct.
  * single-correct: Toggle a, then Toggle a  => selection is empty (re-click still clears).
  * multi-correct:  Toggle a, then Toggle b  => selection is [a,b] (additive preserved); Submit with the
    exact correct set grades Correct, and a strict subset grades Incorrect.

=============================================================================
FIX 2 (verification integrity) -- the browser assertion must walk the learner path
=============================================================================
scripts/browser-check.mjs line ~926 currently does `clickAssert(wrongOpt, 'deselect the wrong quiz
option')` before clicking the correct one. That is why the harness passed while the defect above was
live: my required assertion ("click the wrong option, then click the correct option") turned out to be
satisfiable only by a path no learner takes.

Remove the deselect step. The sequence must be exactly: click the WRONG option -> submit -> assert
#ex-feedback starts "Not quite" and carries class "incorrect" -> click the CORRECT option (NO deselect)
-> submit -> assert #ex-feedback starts "Correct", class "correct", #ex-note visible, #btn-ex-next
present. Update the --self-test static fixture the same way so it models the shipped semantics (its
grader currently accepts only `selectedIds.length === 1 && selectedIds[0] === correctOpt`, which is the
right rule -- it is the driver's extra click that has to go).

--self-test-negative must still report exactly its sabotage-sensitive assertions failing and nothing
else, and the full real run must still be green.

=============================================================================
FIX 3 (verification integrity) -- prove the inventory binding actually fired
=============================================================================
The four id-binding checks are scoped by `isRealContentPath`, a literal "content/exercises/" substring
test on each deck file's path. On the shipped configuration this is CORRECT and I verified it fires: I
swapped a live id for the retired tombstone q-1-14 in the real tree and got
`E-ID-RETIRED ... exit 1`. But the activation is invisible in the report, so any future move of the
content root, a CI that builds from a copied tree, or a rename silently disables four checks with
everything still green. That is the "check that can silently stop checking" pattern this project has
shipped twice.

Make the scope observable and asserted:
  * exercise-check --json's `totals` gains `inventoryChecked`: the number of decks for which the
    id-binding checks were actually applied.
  * check-site.sh asserts, on the real corpus, that `inventoryChecked` equals `totals.decks` (today: 4).
    A run where the binding silently did not apply must turn this RED.
  * Demonstrate it: run exercise-check against a copy of the real content at a path with no
    "content/exercises/" segment, show `inventoryChecked` is 0 there, and show the check-site assertion
    failing when handed that report. Report both outputs.

=============================================================================
FIX 4 (my error) -- restore the cabal cache restore-keys fallback
=============================================================================
My manifest asserted zero whole-file `restore-keys` occurrences in .github/workflows/site.yml. That
assertion was OVERBROAD and I was wrong to write it. It encodes M0 finding M3, which is about the
TOOLCHAIN cache: a broad restore-key there let a stale toolchain be certified as fresh, because
install-toolchain.sh's health check accepted any working compiler. The cabal `site/dist-newstyle` cache
has no equivalent lying health check -- GHC's own recompilation checking is content-based, M1 already
hashes site/src and site/test into the key, addDependentFile covers translations and content, and
check-site.sh's three-way stats agreement plus the per-deck FNV-1a comparison catch residual staleness
behaviourally. Removing that fallback bought no safety and costs a full miso + library rebuild on every
source change in CI.

Restore the cabal dist-newstyle `restore-keys` fallback exactly as the gate-cleared M1 workflow had it,
keeping M1's key composition (including the site/src and site/test hashes). Leave the TOOLCHAIN cache
exact-key-only -- that one stays as it is.

Then fix the assertion that caused this, so nobody re-removes it: whatever check enforced "no
restore-keys" must be narrowed to the toolchain cache block only, and must state in a comment that
restore-keys is forbidden on the toolchain cache (M0 M3) and permitted on the cabal cache. Preserve every
other workflow property: contents:read at workflow scope with pages:write and id-token:write only on
deploy, persist-credentials:false, per-ref build concurrency with group: pages on deploy alone,
timeout-minutes on verification, the deploy gate on vars.ENABLE_PAGES, the result=complete assertion, and
the early exercise-check step.

=============================================================================
DONE LOOKS LIKE
=============================================================================
  * exercise-check --self-test passes with the new Choice-selection cases, and you have SHOWN those cases
    failing against the pre-fix engine (paste both outputs).
  * content-check still 357/357; --fixtures still 51/51; the corpus still reports 0 issues.
  * ./scripts/build-site.sh then ./scripts/check-site.sh: result=complete, and app.wasm's gzip size is
    still under 1,000,000 with WASM_GZIP_CEILING_BYTES untouched. Report the measured size -- the margin
    is ~21 KB and this change should be roughly size-neutral.
  * browser-check.mjs --self-test, --self-test-negative, and a full real run against the served build all
    green with the deselect step gone.
  * Report: the measured gzip before and after, the two engine outputs, the inventoryChecked
    demonstration, and the workflow diff.
